title: The Funnel
subtitle: every provider's result, and its uncertainty, in one picture
name: ModelInMotion_LogisticFE_E15_TheFunnel
status: DRAFT: script under review together with its animatic.

segments.visual: A field of two hundred dots. Six are marked for a moment, three in one colour and three in another, then all look alike again.

sentences.text: Here are two hundred providers, and a secret.
Six of them truly differ from the reference: three worse, three better. The other 194 are, in truth, identical.
sentences.say: Six of them truly differ from the reference: three worse, three better. The other one hundred and ninety-four are, in truth, identical.

segments.visual: The same two hundred as a league table: their ratios in order, from 2.03 on the left to 0.32 on the right.

sentences.text: And here are their ratios, sorted from highest to lowest. A league table.
Can you pick out the six?

segments.visual: The top three and bottom three are boxed. Two turn out to be among the six; the other four are identical providers with 25, 27, 42 and 29 patients.

sentences.text: Take the three at the top and the three at the bottom, and you would be right about two. The other four are identical providers, small ones, having a lucky or an unlucky year.
A league table cannot tell luck from difference. We need a picture that can.

segments.visual: Series logo and wordmark; arc and episode title.

sentences.text: Welcome back to Model in Motion.
Today: the funnel.

segments.visual: Dune's pile from Episode 13, on its axis of counts. The axis is relabelled: each count divided by 4.8, so that it reads as a ratio, with 1 at the centre.

sentences.text: Start with Dune's pile from Episode 13: what luck allows, for a clinic like the reference with Dune's patients.
sentences.say: Start with Dune's pile from Episode thirteen: what luck allows, for a clinic like the reference with Dune's patients.

sentences.text: Divide every count by the 4.8 expected, and the pile sits on the ratio scale, centred on 1.
sentences.say: Divide every count by the four point eight expected, and the pile sits on the ratio scale, centred on one.

segments.visual: A bracket under the pile from 0.38 to 1.62, holding 95% of it. The bracket turns upright and becomes a vertical band.

sentences.text: Keep the stretch that holds 95% of it: from 0.38 to 1.62.
sentences.say: Keep the stretch that holds ninety-five percent of it: from zero point three eight to one point six two.

sentences.text: Stand that band upright. A ratio inside it is unremarkable for Dune.

segments.visual: Two upright bands on one chart, placed by precision: Dune's at 10, from 0.38 to 1.62; Birch's at 39, from 0.69 to 1.31.

sentences.text: How wide the band is depends on how much a clinic can tell us. Call that its precision. Dune's is 10.
sentences.say: How wide the band is depends on how much a clinic can tell us. Call that its precision. Dune's is ten.

sentences.text: Birch has more to go on: a precision of 39, and a narrower band, from 0.69 to 1.31.
sentences.say: Birch has more to go on: a precision of thirty-nine, and a narrower band, from zero point six nine to one point three one.

segments.visual: Bands at many precisions; their upper and lower edges are joined into two curves around the line at 1.

sentences.text: Now do that at every precision, and join the edges.
Wide on the left, where clinics tell us little. Narrow on the right. A funnel.

segments.visual: The five clinics as dots on the funnel: Dune (10.0, 1.46), Cedar (16.7, 1.00) and Birch (39.1, 0.88) inside; Alder (13.0, 1.62) above the upper edge.

sentences.text: Place the cast. Dune, Cedar and Birch sit inside. Alder, at 1.62, is outside.
sentences.say: Place the cast. Dune, Cedar and Birch sit inside. Alder, at one point six two, is outside.

sentences.text: Outside the funnel means flagged, by last episode's bell-curve test. It is the same calculation, drawn.

segments.visual: Elm at precision 2.4 and ratio 0. There the lower edge is at −0.27, below the zero line.

sentences.text: And Elm, far to the left. At Elm's precision the lower edge is below zero. No count, not even none, could flag so small a clinic as better than the reference.

segments.visual: The level crowd on the funnel. Thirteen of the 194 identical providers lie outside and are ringed. A note: over fifty redraws, 4.8% on average.

sentences.text: Now the two hundred from the start. Of the 194 identical providers, 13 fall outside the funnel, by luck alone.
sentences.say: Now the two hundred from the start. Of the one hundred and ninety-four identical providers, thirteen fall outside the funnel, by luck alone.

sentences.text: That is what a 5% line means. Draw the crowd again and again, and on average 5% of them land outside.
sentences.say: That is what a five percent line means. Draw the crowd again and again, and on average five percent of them land outside.

segments.visual: The six who differ are coloured, each labelled with its number of patients. Three are outside; the two with 37 patients and the better one with 105 are inside.

sentences.text: And the six who truly differ? The funnel catches three.
It misses both of the small ones, with 37 patients each. And it misses a better-than-reference provider with 105: a low count is harder to prove than a high one.
sentences.say: It misses both of the small ones, with thirty-seven patients each. And it misses a better-than-reference provider with a hundred and five: a low count is harder to prove than a high one.

segments.visual: Two notes beside the funnel: outside is not a verdict; inside is consistent with the reference, not equal to it.

sentences.text: So a dot outside is not a verdict, and a dot inside is not an acquittal. Inside means consistent with the reference, not equal to it.

segments.visual: Two rows of a hundred risk chips: one with slices of 5%, one with slices of 40%. Their precisions: 5 and 67, marked on the funnel's axis.

sentences.text: Why put precision along the bottom, and not the number of patients?
Take two providers with 100 patients each. One treats patients whose risk is near 5%; the other, near 40%.
sentences.say: Take two providers with a hundred patients each. One treats patients whose risk is near five percent; the other, near forty percent.

sentences.text: Their precisions are 5 and 67. The same size, at opposite ends of the funnel.
sentences.say: Their precisions are five and sixty-seven. The same size, at opposite ends of the funnel.

segments.visual: The crowd's fourteen providers of about a hundred patients, picked out on the funnel: precisions from 19 to 74.

sentences.text: In our crowd, providers of about a hundred patients have precisions from 19 to 74.
sentences.say: In our crowd, providers of about a hundred patients have precisions from nineteen to seventy-four.

segments.visual: The two hundred providers in ratio order, each with its exact interval as a thin vertical line; flagged ones are coloured. A line at 1.

sentences.text: One companion picture. Sort the providers by ratio, and give each one its interval from Episode 13.
sentences.say: One companion picture. Sort the providers by ratio, and give each one its interval from Episode thirteen.

sentences.text: The funnel shows how much each provider can tell us. The caterpillar shows the order, and how little the order can be trusted.

segments.visual: A close-up of the funnel at Dune's precision: the smooth edges at 0.38 and 1.62, and the exact limits at 0.31 and 1.56, half-way between counts.

sentences.text: A footnote on the funnel. With the exact test, each provider has limits of its own, stepping between whole counts. The smooth curve is a guide to them.

segments.visual: The funnel with the level crowd; then the dots move to the series' usual crowd, where providers differ a little. Forty-nine of the 194 are now outside.

sentences.text: One last turn of a knob. Until now, all but six of our providers were identical. Let them truly differ a little, as real providers do.
Now a quarter of the dots are outside the funnel.

segments.visual: A question over the funnel: outliers, or a funnel too narrow?

sentences.text: Is each of them an outlier? Or is the funnel too narrow for a world in which everyone differs? Hold that question. It has an episode of its own.

segments.visual: Three recap cards, each with a small icon.

sentences.text: Let's gather it up.
Up the side, the ratio. Along the bottom, precision: how much a provider can tell us.
The funnel is what luck allows at each precision. Outside it means flagged.
And dots on the left are not worse providers. They are quieter ones.

segments.visual: The funnel, small, resting on a block labelled the risk model; the next episode's title.

sentences.text: Every picture in this act has leaned on something we have not yet questioned: the risk model itself.
Next time: can we trust it?

segments.visual: Series end card with the next episode title.

sentences.text: This has been Model in Motion. Thanks for following the story.
